title: Sovereign Border Regulation vs Open Mobility Rights
rootClaim: Sovereign democratic nation-states possess the moral authority and political duty to restrict immigration and enforce national border controls.

branches.text: Communitarian Social Contract & Public Goods Defense: Welfare state sustainability, civic trust, and public sector capacity require defined, enforceable national boundaries.

children.text: Fiscal Burden & Public Service Strain: High volumes of low-skilled immigration place immediate non-linear pressure on municipal public infrastructure, healthcare systems, and affordable housing.

Net Fiscal Contribution Fallacy: Econometric data demonstrates that immigrants contribute more in lifetime tax revenues than they consume in public services, while counteracting aging demographic trends.

Spatial Localized Disparity: Federal tax gains accrue to central governments, whereas municipal budgets absorb immediate educational and healthcare infrastructure costs without adequate federal reimbursement.
Wage Suppression & Worker Displacement: Uncontrolled expansion of low-skilled labor supply exerts downward pressure on wages for vulnerable domestic workers.

Complementary Labor Hypothesis: Foreign-born workers complement native-born labor rather than substituting it, driving overall economic productivity, lowering consumer prices, and creating new overall jobs.

branches.text: Cosmopolitan Global Justice & Universal Freedom of Movement: National borders are arbitrary products of historical chance; restricting human mobility violates basic human liberty and perpetuates global inequality.

children.text: Rawlsian Global Veil of Ignorance: Rational individuals behind a veil of ignorance would reject national border restrictions that lock millions into geographical poverty and authoritarian oppression.
Self-Determination & Democratic Cohesion: A self-governing political community requires a bounded civic body with shared democratic norms to maintain institutional trust and social welfare consent.
Dynamic Pluralist Integration: Constitutional democracies historically absorb and integrate diverse migrant streams without eroding legal institutions or civic commitment.
Global Economic Surplus: Removing international labor barriers would double global GDP by allocating human capital where it yields highest marginal productivity.

definitions.description: A philosophy emphasizing the connection between the individual and the community, asserting that rights and social obligations depend on bounded political memberships.
The ethical view that all human beings belong to a single global community with equal moral standing regardless of citizenship.
The economic theory that immigrant workers possess skill sets that complement rather than directly compete with native-born workers.
John Rawls's thought experiment where principles of justice are chosen without knowing one's social position, wealth, or place of birth.
